subject: Polity
description: President of India: election, qualifications, powers, removal, tenure

questions.stem: President of India is elected by an ELECTORAL COLLEGE consisting of:

options.option_text: Direct popular vote of all citizens here also too. option used
Elected MPs of both Houses + elected MLAs of states + UTs (Delhi, Puducherry, J&K)
Only Lok Sabha members directly here also too. option used option
Council of Ministers + Chief Justices here also too. option used

questions.explanation: Article 54 — President elected INDIRECTLY by ELECTORAL COLLEGE: (1) ELECTED members of both LS + RS (no nominated members vote); (2) ELECTED members of state legislative assemblies; (3) ELECTED members of LAs of UTs of Delhi, Puducherry, + J&K (added per 70th Amendment, 1992). Voting by SECRET BALLOT, SINGLE TRANSFERABLE VOTE, PROPORTIONAL REPRESENTATION. Each MP/MLA's vote has WEIGHTED VALUE — MLAs based on state population (e.g., UP MLA's vote weight is more than Sikkim MLA's). MP value derived to ensure equal influence with all MLAs combined. INSIGHT: indirect election keeps Pres above partisan popular politics; designed by Constituent Assembly to mirror parliamentary (not presidential) system.

questions.stem: Minimum AGE qualification for President is:
questions.explanation: Article 58 — qualifications: (1) Indian CITIZEN; (2) at least 35 YEARS old; (3) qualified to be a Lok Sabha member; (4) NOT hold any office of profit (under Govt of India / state / local authority — explicit exemptions: PM, ministers, governors, etc.). NOMINATION: 50 proposers + 50 seconders (high threshold to filter casual candidates; raised from 5 in 1997). DEPOSIT: ₹15,000 (forfeited if <1/6 of votes). INSIGHT — same min age (35) for VICE PRESIDENT + GOVERNOR, but: Pres → 5-year term, no formal upper age limit; can be re-elected (no limit on terms — only Rajendra Prasad served 2 full terms; J. Nehru wanted 1 term as norm).
questions.subject: Polity

questions.explanation: Article 56 — term = 5 YEARS from date of taking office. Eligible for RE-ELECTION (no fixed limit). RAJENDRA PRASAD = ONLY president to serve 2 full terms (1950-62). RESIGNATION = addressed to VICE PRESIDENT. REMOVAL: by IMPEACHMENT (Article 61) — for VIOLATION OF CONSTITUTION. Process: charge initiated by EITHER House (1/4 of total membership signature + 14-day notice + 2/3 majority of total membership of that House); other House investigates + must also pass with 2/3 majority. ALL members vote (incl. nominated, EXCLUDED from his ELECTION but INCLUDED in impeachment). India: NO president has ever been impeached. AMERICAN FOUNDING analog: Andrew Johnson (1868), Bill Clinton (1998), Trump (twice, 2019 + 2021) — all acquitted by Senate.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.explanation: DR. RAJENDRA PRASAD (1884-1963) — first President of India; took oath 26 Jan 1950 (Republic Day). Served 2 full terms (1950-62) — only Pres to do so. Earlier presided over CONSTITUENT ASSEMBLY (1946-49). Bharat Ratna 1962. Born in Bihar (Ziradei, Siwan). Educated in Calcutta. Joined Gandhi's freedom movement. Wrote 'India Divided' (1946), 'At the Feet of Mahatma Gandhi' (autobiography). DEMOCRACY ICONS: NEHRU (PM, statesman); PATEL (Iron Man, integrated 565 princely states); AMBEDKAR (constitution architect, dalit rights); RAJAGOPALACHARI (last Governor-General, Bharat Ratna). Subsequent Presidents: Radhakrishnan, Zakir Husain, V.V. Giri, F.A. Ahmed (died in office, 1977), N.S. Reddy, Zail Singh, Venkataraman, S.D. Sharma, K.R. Narayanan, A.P.J. Abdul Kalam, Pratibha Patil (first woman, 2007-12), Pranab Mukherjee, Ram Nath Kovind, DROUPADI MURMU (current, 2022-, first tribal woman).

questions.stem: President is the SUPREME COMMANDER of:

options.option_text: All police forces of all states

questions.explanation: Article 53(2) — Supreme Command of DEFENCE FORCES (Army, Navy, Air Force) vested in PRESIDENT; exercised IN ACCORDANCE WITH LAW (i.e., on advice of council of ministers led by PM, who acts via Defence Minister + military chiefs). Symbolic role — President doesn't direct military operations day-to-day. President APPOINTS service chiefs (CDS, COAS, CNS, CAS). DECLARES war + concludes peace (per advice of Cabinet). PARDONS courts-martial (Article 72). NOT supreme over police (state subject under STATE LIST except in UTs). PARA-MILITARY (CRPF, BSF, ITBP, CISF) under Home Ministry. Comparable: US President is C-in-C of US Armed Forces under their Constitution.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: President can grant PARDONS, REPRIEVES, etc. under which Article?
questions.explanation: Article 72 — gives President the power to grant: PARDON (full forgiveness; person treated innocent); COMMUTATION (substitute milder sentence — e.g., death → life); REMISSION (reduce punishment without changing nature — e.g., 10 yrs → 7 yrs); RESPITE (lesser sentence due to special circumstances — e.g., pregnancy, age); REPRIEVE (temporary stay, esp. of execution, while a final decision is reached). Pres has WIDER powers than GOVERNOR (Article 161): Pres can pardon DEATH SENTENCES + COURT-MARTIAL cases too. Mercy petition reaches Pres after all judicial appeals exhausted. Pres is BOUND by Cabinet's advice (post 42nd Amendment); but can return for reconsideration (44th Amendment). FAMOUS CASES: Afzal Guru (rejected 2013); Yakub Memon (rejected 2015); Nirbhaya convicts (rejected 2020).

questions.stem: Who can act as President when both President + Vice President offices are VACANT?
questions.explanation: If both PRES + VP offices vacant simultaneously: CHIEF JUSTICE OF INDIA (CJI) acts as President. If CJI also vacant, NEXT senior-most SC judge acts. Until new Pres + VP elected within 6 months. ACTUAL CASE: 1969 — Pres ZAKIR HUSAIN died in office (3 May 1969). VP V.V. GIRI became acting Pres (24 hrs after Husain's death). Giri then RESIGNED VP to contest Pres election. M. HIDAYATULLAH (CJI) ACTED as President from 20 July to 24 Aug 1969 — only such instance. Got narrow resolution from Cabinet to assume the role. Subsequent: Giri won + became 4th President. INSIGHT: Constitution has a clear succession ladder — VP → CJI → next SC judge — to ensure continuity.
